title: Bounded module-cache cleanup v2
objective: Make automatic compiler module-cache cleanup identity-safe, promptly retryable, bounded for oversized eligible generations, and quietly observable while preserving every current safety invariant

oracles: Deterministic filesystem concurrency and retention tests

handoff.summary: Automatic module-cache maintenance now uses a portable atomic-mkdir directory lock with an owner token, identity-safe stale removal, and conservative migration of stale regular-file locks from the previous protocol. Work-limited passes may remove one oversized eligible generation and record a shorter retry deadline whenever work remains or a pass fails. State publication is atomic, startup remains silent, and `sagejs cache status [--json]` exposes the last result and next deadline. Deterministic fixtures cover two-process stale-lock contention, legacy migration, oversized progress, deferred retry scheduling, protected generations, unsafe markers, and status output.
risks: Like the existing advisory lease protocol, reclaiming an owner whose token has not changed for longer than the stale timeout assumes that owner is dead rather than paused.

The final broad build was disrupted by a separately identified concurrent dist/module-cache-build deletion race; focused TypeScript and cache tests are fresh, while compiler and integration suites require revalidation after the shared build-cache repair lands.
next_steps: Merge the shared compiler/build-cache repair, then rerun pnpm build, pnpm test:compiler, and pnpm test:integration before integration.
Exercise the directory-lock tests on native Windows CI, where mkdir/rmdir are the intended portable synchronization primitives.
